title: Google Teachable Machine
description: This tool provides a simple interface for creating machine learning models without requiring coding experience. Setup time is minimal, making it suitable for introductory AI exploration.

• Compare model performance using different quantities of training samples (few vs many).
  • Adjust parameters such as epochs, batch size, and learning rate to observe their impact on accuracy and loss.
  • Investigate dataset bias or imbalance (e.g., training on only one color of object may reduce generalization).
  • Test model robustness by introducing noise into image or audio inputs.

This tool is well suited for introductory machine learning lessons and supports a wide range of classroom experiments focused on data, training, and model behavior. Project files can be opened through the platform using the built-in import feature.

title: Introduction to AI-Assisted Coding
description: This activity explores AI-assisted programming through the recreation of a Connections-style game. The original online IDE environment was unavailable, so the assignment was rebuilt as a standalone web project.

The exercise is designed to support learning in prompt engineering and code analysis. A structured approach can be used where students generate code using AI once, then focus on debugging and improving the output independently.

Two prompt variations are included in the download folder for comparison: a simple prompt and a detailed prompt. The outputs were analyzed to evaluate differences in structure, completeness, and required debugging effort.
This activity is suitable for both beginner and intermediate learners and can also serve as an introduction to web development concepts and AI-assisted workflow design.

title: Interactive Transformer Visualization of GPT-2
description: This tool visualizes how transformer-based language models generate text one token at a time, illustrating the step-by-step prediction process.
The interface includes explanatory text that describes how the model processes input and produces output. The main adjustable parameter is temperature, which controls randomness in token selection.
Suggested classroom applications include converting the explanation into guided slides or having students construct sentences while observing model behavior.

Additional resources include a 'Tokenizer Visualizer' and a lecture on transformers which provide further insight into model structure and token processing. Included files consist of screenshots of these tools.

title: Artificial Neuron
description: This guided activity introduces the concept of artificial neurons through interactive explanations and embedded quizzes. It focuses on foundational machine learning concepts such as inputs, weights, and bias.
The activity is designed to support conceptual understanding rather than advanced technical implementation, making it suitable for introductory learners.
Assessment can be supported through documentation or screenshot-based submissions of completed activities.
Supplementary materials include screenshots of the activity and related external resources that reinforce the concept of neural computation.

This website on 'How to Think Like a Neuron' is similar to this activity. It provides an additional perspective on neural network concepts and reinforces understanding of how artificial neurons process information.

title: API Explorer - Class Activity
description: This interactive activity introduces students to working with APIs using JavaScript fetch requests. It provides a sandbox environment where users can modify API calls and observe real-time JSON responses.

• Practice using query parameters to filter and sort data (e.g., category, platform, popularity).
  • Learn how to retrieve a single resource using path parameters (e.g., fetching a game by ID).
  • Understand how API keys work by testing requests with and without authentication.
  • Explore error handling by comparing valid and invalid requests and analyzing status codes.

The activity is well suited for introductory web development or computer science courses and reinforces core concepts such as client-server communication, JSON data structures, and debugging API responses.

title: Godot 4 Multiplayer Tutorial
description: This tutorial demonstrates how to create a basic 3D multiplayer game in Godot 4 using built-in networking tools. It walks through setting up a host and client system, spawning players, and synchronizing gameplay across multiple instances.

• Host and join system using ENet multiplayer peer.
  • Player spawning with MultiplayerSpawner.
  • RPCs for syncing and removing players.
  • Position and rotation sync with MultiplayerSynchronizer.
This tutorial is best suited for intermediate users who already understand basic Godot concepts and want to learn how multiplayer networking works..

title: Intro to Computer Science
description: A self-paced introductory course covering the fundamentals of computer science and programming.

• Binary Module: How computers store and process data using 0s and 1s.
  • Logic Module: How computers use boolean values to make decisions.
  • Hardware Module: evolution of computers and how software runs on physical systems.
Designed for complete beginners with no prior experience, introducing core concepts that underpin all modern computing.

title: Autoencoder Reconstruction Colab
description: A hands-on lab where you build and train an autoencoder using PyTorch to reconstruct MNIST handwritten digits.

• Encoder: Compresses 28×28 images into a low-dimensional latent vector representation.
  • Bottleneck (Latent Space): The compressed representation that controls how much information is preserved; smaller dimensions increase compression but reduce detail.
  • Decoder: Reconstructs the original image from the latent vector.
  • Training Exploration: Students modify epochs, batch size, learning rate, and latent dimension to observe effects on reconstruction quality.
Focuses on understanding how compression affects reconstruction quality, loss behavior (MSE), and the trade-off between model capacity and information loss.

title: Slide Deck Archive
description: A collection of miscellaneous lecture PowerPoint slide decks and classroom presentation materials grouped into a single archive page.
All slides are in .pdf format.

title: Cheat Sheets Archive
description: A collection of miscellaneous cheat sheets and reference documents grouped into a single archive page.

title: TicTacToe Project
description: A beginner-friendly Tic Tac Toe programming activity designed for introductory computer science students using Python.
Students complete missing sections of code by replacing fill-in-the-blank placeholders throughout the program.

• Create and manage a 2D game board using lists.
  • Validate user input and detect invalid moves.
  • Place markers and update game state.
  • Check for winning conditions across rows, columns, and diagonals.
  • Detect draw conditions and control the main game loop.

title: Personal Website Project
description: A React-based project where students customize and deploy a personal portfolio website using a pre-made template.

• Edit React components such as About, Hero, Contact, Footer, and Projects.
  • Update personal information, links, images, and resume files.
  • Deploy the website publicly using Vercel and GitHub.
The activity introduces students to React development, GitHub workflows, and modern website deployment.

title: Hugging Face
description: Hugging Face is a machine learning teaching platform that allows users to explore, run, and train AI models for text, image, audio, and multimodal tasks. Beginners can use pretrained models with minimal coding, while advanced learners can fine-tune and deploy state-of-the-art models.

• Compare model outputs using different prompts, datasets, and inference settings.
  • Learn machine learning workflows including tokenization, datasets, training, evaluation, and deployment.
  • Deep RL Course, ML for Games Course, Intro to AI Course, LLM Course, etc.
  • Free datasets that can be used for Python projects.
Free tutorials (like this QuickStart Guide) and courses are available through the Hugging Face learning portal.

title: Google AI Studio
description: Google AI Studio is a free browser-based platform for experimenting with Gemini models using prompts, chat, and multimodal inputs.

• Compare outputs using different prompts and temperature settings.
  • Generate structured JSON outputs using response schemas.
  • Upload images, audio, PDFs, and text files for multimodal prompting.
  • Test basic grounding and retrieval workflows with external context.
AI Studio will not teach students backpropagation, gradient descent, loss functions, activation functions, or attention mechanisms. They are interacting with a 'black box.'

title: OpenAI Developers
description: OpenAI Developers is a learning and documentation platform for building applications with OpenAI models using APIs and developer tools.

• Building agents (1–3 hours, Beginner): Learn foundational concepts and build simple agent systems using tool use and step-by-step workflows.
  • AI app development: Concept to production (2–4 hours, Intermediate): Build, deploy, and optimize AI applications from prototype to working product.
  • Model optimization (1–2 hours, Advanced): Explore fine-tuning, distillation, and techniques for improving performance and cost efficiency.
Includes structured courses plus a large collection of documentation, guides, API references, and developer tools for building real-world AI systems. Some API usage may require paid credits.

title: MNIST Neural Network Visualizer
description: An interactive browser-based neural network trainer for MNIST number classification where students can modify model settings and observe learning in real time.

• Train a neural network on handwritten digit classification and watch predictions improve over time.
  • Modify architecture and hyperparameters (e.g., layers, learning rate) and observe changes in performance.
  • Test model behavior by drawing digits and analyzing prediction confidence.
This tool focuses on real-time training behavior of neural networks, making concepts like learning dynamics, convergence, and misclassification observable directly in the browser.

title: CNN Explainer
description: Explains what convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are and how they process images.

• Visualizes convolution filters detecting features like edges and textures.
  • Shows pooling layers reducing spatial size while retaining key information.
  • Displays feature maps across layers.
  • Demonstrates how extracted features are used for classification.
Combines conceptual explanations with interactive CNN visualization.

title: SUMMIT Interactive Visualization
description: Interactive system for visualizing and summarizing learned features in deep neural networks.

• Aggregates neuron activations to identify important features.
  • Visualizes relationships between neurons using attribution graphs.
  • Shows how learned features contribute to predictions.
  • Explores model behavior on large datasets like ImageNet.
Designed to help users understand how deep learning models make predictions at scale.

title: TensorFlow Neural Network Playground
description: Interactive tool for building and training simple neural networks in the browser.

• Train networks on toy datasets and visualize decision boundaries.
  • Adjust layers, neurons, activation functions, learning rate, and regularization.
  • Observe how parameter changes affect convergence and accuracy.
  • Compare model performance across different dataset patterns.
Explains neural networks as layered systems of connected units that learn by strengthening or weakening connections based on error feedback.

title: PyTorch Tutorials
description: Official PyTorch tutorials and learning resources covering deep learning fundamentals, model training, deployment, and advanced AI workflows using the PyTorch framework.

• Build and train neural networks using tensors, datasets, autograd, and optimization tools.
  • Learn computer vision workflows including CNNs, image classification, and transfer learning.
  • Explore natural language processing and transformer-based models.
  • Practice model deployment, GPU acceleration, and production workflows.
The tutorials range from beginner-friendly introductions to advanced implementation guides and are widely used for hands-on machine learning and deep learning education.

title: GAN Lab
description: Interactive browser-based tool for visualizing how Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) train and generate data.

• Visualizes generator and discriminator behavior in real time.
  • Adjust hyperparameters and observe training changes instantly.
  • Explore datasets, gradients, decision boundaries, and generated samples.
Useful for teaching/understanding GANs, adversarial training, and generative AI concepts without requiring installation.

title: ConvNetJS
description: Browser-based JavaScript deep learning library with interactive neural network demos and educational resources.

• Includes demos for MNIST, CIFAR-10, autoencoders, reinforcement learning, and neural network visualization.
  • Contains a brief introduction to deep learning and neural networks.
  • Provides Getting Started guides and documentation for building and training models.
Useful for learning and experimenting with deep learning directly in the browser without installation.

title: What-If Tool
description: Interactive tool for analyzing and visualizing machine learning model predictions directly in the browser.

• Includes built-in demos and tutorials for exploring model behavior and interpretability.
  • Explore classification results, confidence scores, and decision boundaries.
  • Modify feature values to test how predictions change.
  • Investigate dataset bias, fairness, and model behavior.
Useful for teaching model interpretability, debugging, fairness, and responsible AI concepts.

title: Google Visual Blocks for ML
description: Visual Blocks for ML is a browser-based visual programming platform developed by Google for building machine learning and AI workflows using drag-and-drop blocks instead of traditional code.

• Create AI workflows by connecting models, inputs, processors, APIs, and outputs in a node-based editor.
  • Prototype multimodal applications involving text, images, audio, and machine learning models.
  • Experiment with LLM chains, computer vision pipelines, and AI-assisted workflows.
  • Build and test AI systems visually without requiring advanced programming experience.

title: Machine Learning  (Block-Based Programming)
description: A browser-based platform for creating and training machine learning models using simple interfaces designed for educational use.

• Train classification models using text, image, number, or sound datasets.
  • Use trained models in Scratch projects to build interactive games and applications, or connect models to other coding environments.
  • Experiment with how training data quality and quantity affect model performance and generalization.
  • Explore full workflows from data collection to training and deployment in beginner-friendly formats.
Additional resources include a worksheets section for guided activities and a pretrained models section for experimenting with ready-made AI models.
After logging in, you will also be able to explore datasets (Titanic Survivors, Phishing Email Prediction, Recognize Song Genres) that you can import here.

title: Snap! (Block-Based Programming)
description: Snap! is a browser-based block programming language developed at UC Berkeley that extends the Scratch-style interface with more advanced programming features.

• Create programs using drag-and-drop blocks for logic, loops, variables, and functions.
  • Build custom blocks to define reusable behaviors and more advanced control structures.
  • Develop interactive games, simulations, and learning projects directly in the browser.
For more details on using Snap! to add AI elements to your projects please reference this GitHub page.

title: MIT App Inventor
description: A set of beginner tutorials for MIT App Inventor that teach how to build simple mobile apps using block-based programming.

• Learn the basics of building Android/iOS apps using drag-and-drop blocks.
  • Follow guided tutorials such as Hello Codi, Ball Bounce, and Digital Doodle.
  • Understand core app components like buttons, sensors, text-to-speech, and screen interaction.
  • Build and test working mobile apps step by step in a browser-based environment.

title: Dify AI
description: Dify AI is a platform for building and deploying LLM-based applications using visual workflows and low-code tools.

• Design AI applications such as chatbots, assistants, and RAG systems using a visual workflow builder.
  • Manage prompts, datasets, and model configurations in a single development environment.
  • Build agent-based systems with tool use, retrieval, and API integrations.
  • Deploy and monitor AI applications with built-in logging and testing tools.
This YouTube tutorial walks through setting up two simple AI chatbots in Dify, demonstrating how to configure prompts, connect models, and deploy a working application step by step.
This document from Dify AI shows you how to get started.

title: Movie Recommender in Python with Google Colab
description: A beginner-friendly project for building a movie recommendation system using Python and Google Colab.

• Load and process MovieLens datasets using pandas.
  • Create movie recommendations using similarity metrics.
  • Build and test a simple Flask API.
  • Students can experiment after completion with larger MovieLens datasets such as 10M or 20M.
Students can expand the project by using the older MovieLens 100K dataset and incorporating user demographic data as an additional challenge.

title: Weather Web App
description: A beginner-friendly weather web application project where students build a responsive interface that retrieves and displays live weather information using a public API.

• Learn how to fetch and process JSON data from a weather API.
  • Create a search feature that allows users to look up weather conditions by city.
  • Display weather information such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and icons dynamically using JavaScript.
  • Practice working with HTML, CSS, and event-driven programming concepts.

title: GeeksforGeeks Python Projects
description: A large collection of Python project ideas and tutorials covering beginner to advanced computer science topics including automation, AI, web development, computer vision, and data processing. Some projects worth noting are:

• Vehicle Detection using OpenCV introduces computer vision concepts for detecting moving vehicles in video frames.
  • Morse Code Translator is a beginner-friendly project focused on string processing and dictionaries.
  • Web Scraping with Beautiful Soup is especially useful because it can support data collection for many other programming and AI projects.
  • Target Detection in a Live Camera Feed explores real-time computer vision and object tracking concepts.

title: Figma Design Project Ideas
description: A collection of computer science project ideas organized into beginner, intermediate, and advanced categories.

• Beginner: CRUD apps, forms, layouts, and basic UI patterns.
  • Intermediate: APIs, data persistence, and multi-screen applications.
  • Advanced: Multi-user systems, integrations, and production-level projects.
The resource mainly provides UI/UX templates and project inspiration rather than complete implementations.
